column1: Section B. Core API transport layer

column2: Implement the eight MSP REST API endpoints
column3: Implement all eight documented endpoints: outbound /message, inbound /message, /preDownload, /preUpload, the returned upload URL, /decodePayload, /authenticate, and /constructPayload.
column4: All endpoints under mspgw.push.apple.com use HTTPS. The inbound /message endpoint is hosted by the MSP at a URL registered with Apple; the rest are Apple-hosted. /constructPayload is required even if App Clips RichLinks are not heavily used.

column2: Implement HS256 JWT signing with 1-hour rotation
column3: Sign every outbound request with an HS256 JWT using the Messaging API secret. iat must be within the last hour at the receiving end.
column4: alg is fixed at HS256. iss is the MSP ID on outbound; aud is the MSP ID on inbound (from Apple). Apple rejects tokens with iat older than 1 hour, so cache and rotate tokens accordingly. Reject inbound JWTs that fail signature, iat freshness, or aud match.

column2: Set every required HTTP header on every outbound message
column3: Populate Authorization, id, Source-Id, Destination-Id, Content-Type, and the message-type-specific headers (e.g. interactive headers, attachment headers) on every outbound request.
column4: Headers are message-type dependent. Interactive messages require additional headers above the standard set. Attachment flows require the encryption headers on /preUpload and /preDownload. Missing headers cause the message to be rejected silently in some cases.

column2: Populate the common HTTP body fields correctly
column3: Every outbound message body must carry the common fields (id, sourceId, destinationId, type, plus the type-specific payload).

column2: Implement GZIP request body handling on inbound
column3: Inbound webhook requests from Apple may arrive gzip-compressed. The MSP must decompress before parsing.

column3: Every inbound request must pass: JWT signature verification, JWT iat freshness check (within 1 hour), required header presence, body schema validation, and id uniqueness / replay protection.
column4: Apple expects all five checks. Failure to enforce iat freshness or id uniqueness is a common review finding. Keep a short-window id replay cache (1 hour matches the iat window).

column3: Apple's webhook traffic originates from the 17.0.0.0/8 CIDR. Restrict the inbound /message endpoint to that range at the edge.
column4: Apply at the WAF or load balancer, not inside the application. 17.0.0.0/8 is an Apple-owned block but is large; combine with JWT verification for defence in depth.

column2: Honour the Opaque ID identity model
column3: sourceId and destinationId on organic AMB are opaque tokens issued by Apple. Never treat them as, transform them into, or persist them alongside, real-world identifiers (phone, email, customer ID) outside of an authenticated linkage.
column4: Opaque IDs are stable per user-brand pair but are not reversible. Logging or analytics pipelines that flatten sourceId into a join key against PII break Apple's privacy contract. Account linking happens via the channel settings landing page, not via id parsing.

column3: Detect inbound user tapbacks (Loved, Liked, Disliked, Laughed, Emphasized, Questioned) including on interactive payloads, plus stickers and emoji reactions.

Correlation is best effort from the body text only: standard reactions quote the original text, and interactive-message reactions collapse to 'Liked 1 Business Message', which identifies no specific message. Parsing is locale dependent. Per Apple, display the received text as is.

column3: Send Apple Pay payment requests with merchant session handoff, ApplePayPaymentRequest payload, line items, shipping methods, and refund handling.Apple Pay requires the Merchant ID registered on the AMB account before sending a request
column4:
For testing,  MSP must have a brand that holds its own Apple Developer account and Apple Pay Merchant ID, not the third-party payment processor's. Payment Processing Certificate enrolment is multi-day. Refunds are handled in a workflow outside Messages for Business. Refund handling is not an in-band AMB feature and is not required within the Apple Pay message

The brand (merchant) owns the Apple Developer account and Apple Pay Merchant ID and shares the Payment Processing Certificate with the MSP. The MSP does not need to hold the processor's enrolments.

Role split: Apple tokenizes the card and issues the merchant session; the MSP transports and authenticates the messages and routes them to the configured endpoints; the brand's own payment gateway and PSP process the charge. Apple Pay in AMB is the presentment and tokenization layer, not the processor. 

Prerequisites: Apple Developer account and Apple Pay Merchant ID configured
Merchant ID must be on the AMB account first.

column3: Use /constructPayload to generate App Clips (a), Apple Maps (b), and Apple Music (c) RichLink payloads server side from a URL. Each of the three payload types must be demonstrated.
column4:
Required even if these RichLink types are not a primary surface for the brand. The API is the only supported way to construct the payload; do not assemble it client side. All three types (App Clips, Apple Maps, Apple Music) are in scope and each must be demonstrated. The demonstration must use a working App Clip URL as evidence.
One example is: https://firigames.com/phoenix2

Apple Music is a Construct Payload rich link built server side via /constructPayload from a music.apple.com URL. Supported content types: Song, Album, Artist, Playlist, Music Video, Radio Station. Match the storefront to the user by constructing the URL dynamically from the incoming message's locale rather than hardcoding a country code, so full rendering including the play button works. It is one of three Construct Payload types (App Clips, Apple Maps, Apple Music) that each must be demonstrated for Apple review.

column2: Routing based on entry point parameters
column3: Use the intentID and groupID attributes on inbound conversation-start messages to route to the correct queue, bot flow, or agent skill.
column4: BCRW (bcrw.apple.com) is the Business Chat era redirect endpoint that turns a URL into a Messages for Business conversation: https://bcrw.apple.com/urn:biz:<business-id>, with optional query parameters biz-intent-id, biz-group-id, and body. On the first inbound message, the MSP reads the intent and group to route the conversation. Parameter values must not contain reserved URI characters (& # [] () {} and /). Note: Apple does not publish the full BCRW acronym expansion, so describe it by function rather than asserting one

column2: Invitation messages with explicit consent, decline, no-response, opt-out, and undeliverable states
column3: Preserve Apple-managed templates, phone-number addressing, gated approval, platform floors, and response-code semantics. Model pending, accepted, declined/No, no-response, opt-out, user-preference-undeliverable, and sender/transport-error states distinctly. When the user selects No, no conversation message or opaque user ID is delivered for display in the MSP platform and the platform MUST NOT continue messaging. Conversational sending becomes eligible only after the user initiates a new conversation.
column4: Invitation 410 is a missing/incorrect `message-type` header, not opt-out. User-preference undeliverable is 404. Do not invent an opaque-ID-to-phone join. Store pre-conversation suppression per brand and normalized destination. A later user-initiated conversation restores conversational reply eligibility but does not automatically recreate campaign or notification consent.

column3: Implement and respect the response code taxonomy: 2xx success, 4xx client errors (including 410 Gone with two distinct semantics on organic AMB vs Invitations), and 5xx server errors with a documented retry policy.

410 Gone on organic AMB means the user is no longer reachable on the channel; on Invitations it means the user has opted out of that specific brand's invitation templates. Treat them as distinct states in the MSP data model.
The published /message codes are 200, 400, 401, 403, 404, 410, 500; Apple documents no 429 for AMB, so any rate-limit handling is an MSP-side inference (see DR-15). On organic AMB, 410 means the user closed the conversation; 'no longer reachable' is 404. On Invitations, 410 means a missing or incorrect message-type header. Treat these as distinct states in the MSP data model
